source_title: Time Series Momentum
author_if_known: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
instrument: 58 liquid futures/forwards across equity indices, currencies, commodities (incl. gold) and government bonds
original_claim_summary: Across 58 futures/forward instruments spanning multiple asset classes, the sign and magnitude of a market's own trailing 12-month excess return positively predicts its excess return over the subsequent month, and this pattern is present for nearly every instrument tested individually.
claimed_mechanism: trend persistence: a sustained directional move over roughly a year tends to continue into the near-term future (own-asset time-series momentum)
context: holds across asset classes and time periods 1965-2009 in the original sample; effect is strongest following large absolute past moves
prerequisite_state: a measurable 12-month trailing excess return (positive or negative) in the instrument
event_sequence: 12-month directional trend established -> holding period begins -> return over next 1-12 months continues in same direction as the trailing trend
trigger: sign of trailing 12-month excess return crossing zero
invalidation: trailing 12-month return near zero (no established trend) or after ~12-36 months when the trend historically begins to partially reverse
claimed_outcome: positive expected return when trading in the direction of the trailing 12-month sign, pooled across instruments and time
falsification_condition: If the sign of trailing 12-month excess return showed no statistically significant relationship to next-month excess return out of sample across the instrument panel, the claim would be false.

source_title: Time Series Momentum
author_if_known: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
instrument: 58 liquid futures/forwards across equity indices, currencies, commodities (incl. gold) and government bonds
original_claim_summary: The time-series momentum effect documented over 1-12 month horizons partially reverses over the subsequent 12-24 months, a pattern the authors interpret as consistent with initial underreaction followed by delayed overreaction and correction.
claimed_mechanism: momentum decay and partial mean-reversion at longer horizons following an initial trend-following phase
context: measured in the pooled diversified time-series momentum portfolio across the 58-instrument panel
prerequisite_state: a completed 1-12 month momentum phase already in place
event_sequence: trend continuation for ~12 months -> deceleration -> partial reversal of cumulative gains over months 13-36
trigger: elapsed time since trend initiation exceeding roughly one year
invalidation: no reversal observed in the 13-36 month window following the trend
claimed_outcome: part of the earlier trend-following profit is given back over the following one to two years
falsification_condition: If cumulative time-series momentum returns kept compounding without reversal (or reversed immediately rather than after ~12+ months) in out-of-sample data, the claim would be false.

source_title: An Investigation of Transactions Data for NYSE Stocks
author_if_known: Robert A. Wood, Thomas H. McInish, J. Keith Ord
original_claim_summary: Average intraday stock returns follow a U-shape across the trading session: significantly positive returns cluster in the first 30 minutes after the open and again near the close, with lower average returns in the middle of the day.
claimed_mechanism: time-of-day conditioning of realized returns tied to the open and close of the session
context: regular NYSE trading hours, aggregate/cross-sectional average across listed common stocks
event_sequence: market open -> elevated average returns in first 30 minutes -> quieter midday drift -> elevated average returns into the close
trigger: proximity to session open or session close
invalidation: flat or randomly distributed intraday average-return profile with no elevation at open/close
claimed_outcome: higher average realized return concentrated at the open and close relative to midday
falsification_condition: If average intraday returns were flat or higher at midday than at the open/close across a broad equity sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: An Investigation of Transactions Data for NYSE Stocks
author_if_known: Robert A. Wood, Thomas H. McInish, J. Keith Ord
original_claim_summary: First-order serial autocorrelation of intraday returns also traces a crude U-shape across the trading day, differing systematically between the open, midday, and close, indicating the return-generating process itself changes with time of day rather than being stationary.
claimed_mechanism: time-varying microstructure/autocorrelation regime across the trading session (non-stationary intraday return process)
context: regular NYSE session, transaction-level data aggregated into intervals
event_sequence: session progresses from open to close -> autocorrelation structure of returns shifts systematically with time-of-day
trigger: time elapsed since open / time remaining to close
invalidation: constant, time-invariant autocorrelation across the session
claimed_outcome: the statistical character of price changes (not just their level) depends on time of day
falsification_condition: If return autocorrelation were statistically indistinguishable across open, midday and close periods, the claim would be false.

source_title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
author_if_known: Yakov Amihud
original_claim_summary: Expected stock illiquidity (measured as average daily absolute return per dollar of volume) is positively related to expected stock returns over time, i.e. periods and stocks with higher illiquidity command a higher return premium.
claimed_mechanism: illiquidity risk premium: compensation demanded by investors for the price impact of trading in less liquid conditions
context: cross-section and time series of NYSE stocks; effect more pronounced in small-cap names
prerequisite_state: elevated Amihud illiquidity ratio (absolute return / dollar volume) relative to history
event_sequence: illiquidity rises -> required/expected return rises -> asset repriced downward until higher forward return is consistent with the higher illiquidity
trigger: increase in the illiquidity ratio
invalidation: no relationship between illiquidity level and subsequent realized/expected returns
claimed_outcome: higher expected returns priced into less liquid stocks and time periods
falsification_condition: If stocks/periods with higher measured illiquidity did not show higher subsequent expected returns after controlling for other risk factors, the claim would be false.

source_title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
author_if_known: Yakov Amihud
original_claim_summary: Unexpected (contemporaneous) increases in market illiquidity are associated with negative contemporaneous stock returns and coincide with periods of elevated volatility, i.e. liquidity evaporation and volatility spikes tend to occur together.
claimed_mechanism: liquidity-volatility feedback: a liquidity shock depresses prices in real time and coincides with heightened volatility
context: periods of market-wide stress where liquidity dries up
prerequisite_state: a shock that reduces trading liquidity
event_sequence: liquidity shock hits -> dollar volume falls / price impact rises -> contemporaneous negative return and higher realized volatility
trigger: unexpected rise in the illiquidity ratio relative to its expected level
invalidation: illiquidity shocks with no associated contemporaneous price decline or volatility increase
claimed_outcome: negative contemporaneous return and elevated volatility concurrent with the liquidity shock
falsification_condition: If unexpected illiquidity increases showed no correlation with contemporaneous negative returns or volatility spikes, the claim would be false.

source_title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market
author_if_known: Carlo Zarattini, Andrea Barbon, Andrew Aziz
instrument: Leveraged US equity ETFs (e.g. TQQQ), 5-minute opening range
original_claim_summary: A systematic opening-range breakout strategy that enters in the direction of the first 5-minute candle's break, uses an ATR-derived stop, and exits at market close, produced statistically significant net-of-cost alpha versus buy-and-hold over a multi-year sample.
claimed_mechanism: opening-range breakout continuation: the direction established by the first few minutes of trading tends to continue for the remainder of the session often enough to be exploitable after volatility-scaled risk control
context: high-volatility leveraged ETFs; day-trading horizon with a hard same-day exit
prerequisite_state: price breaks above/below the high/low of the opening 5-minute range
event_sequence: opening 5-minute range forms -> price breaks the range high or low -> position taken in breakout direction -> held to close or ATR-based stop
trigger: close of a 5-minute bar beyond the opening range high/low
invalidation: price reverts back inside the opening range and hits the ATR-based stop before the close
claimed_outcome: positive risk-adjusted return net of realistic transaction costs and slippage over the sample period
falsification_condition: If the same 5-minute ORB rule applied out-of-sample to a new period produced no statistically significant edge net of realistic costs, the claim would be false.

source_title: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? Evidence of Sustainable Long-Term Profits from Opening Range Breakout (ORB) Day Trading Strategy vs. Benchmark in the US Stock Market
author_if_known: Andrew Aziz, Carlo Zarattini
original_claim_summary: Opening-range breakout profitability is concentrated in stocks showing abnormally elevated relative trading volume/news catalysts ("stocks in play"); restricting the ORB signal to this subset materially improves results versus applying it to the broad, unfiltered stock universe.
claimed_mechanism: breakout continuation is conditional on elevated participation/liquidity and information flow, not a universal property of any range break
context: requires a volume/news filter to isolate stocks with abnormal same-day activity before applying the breakout rule
prerequisite_state: stock is flagged as having relative volume or news catalyst well above its own historical baseline
event_sequence: screen for abnormal relative volume/news -> opening range forms -> breakout of the range -> continuation more reliable than in an unfiltered universe
trigger: range breakout occurring specifically within the pre-filtered high-activity subset
invalidation: breakout occurring in a stock without abnormal volume/news showing materially worse continuation odds
claimed_outcome: higher win rate / return per trade for filtered vs. unfiltered ORB signals
falsification_condition: If ORB win rate/return were statistically indistinguishable between the volume-filtered subset and the broad unfiltered universe, the claim would be false.

source_title: Market Intraday Momentum
author_if_known: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
original_claim_summary: The market's return in the first 30 minutes of trading (since the prior close) positively and significantly predicts the return in the last 30 minutes of the same trading day, with a scaled slope of about 6.94 and R-squared near 1.6%.
claimed_mechanism: intraday momentum: early-session directional information is only partially impounded and continues to push price in the same direction into the close
context: regular US equity trading session; effect measured on a highly liquid, broad index ETF
prerequisite_state: a measurable first-30-minute return since the prior close
event_sequence: first 30 minutes of session establish a directional return -> midday -> last 30 minutes tend to continue in the same direction
trigger: sign and magnitude of the opening 30-minute return
invalidation: no statistically significant relationship between opening and closing half-hour returns
claimed_outcome: positive, statistically significant predictive relationship between first and last half-hour returns
falsification_condition: If the first-half-hour return showed no statistically significant predictive slope on the last-half-hour return out of sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: Market Intraday Momentum
author_if_known: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
instrument: S&P 500 ETF (SPY) plus 10 other liquid domestic/international ETFs
original_claim_summary: The intraday momentum effect (first half-hour predicting last half-hour) is stronger on days with higher realized volatility, higher trading volume, during economic recessions, and on days with major macroeconomic news releases.
claimed_mechanism: regime-conditioned intraday momentum: predictability of late-session direction from early-session direction increases with informational/volatility intensity of the day
context: high-volatility, high-volume, recessionary, or macro-news days show stronger effect than average/quiet days
prerequisite_state: day is classified as high volatility, high volume, recession, or macro-announcement day
event_sequence: day begins with elevated volatility/volume or scheduled macro news -> first half-hour return recorded -> predictive relationship to last half-hour strengthens versus an average day
trigger: day-level classification as high-activity (volatility/volume/news/recession)
invalidation: predictive slope not meaningfully different between high-activity and quiet days
claimed_outcome: amplified predictability of the last half-hour return conditional on elevated day-level activity
falsification_condition: If the intraday momentum slope were flat (not stronger) on high-volatility/high-volume/news days relative to quiet days, the claim would be false.

source_title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
author_if_known: David O. Lucca, Emanuel Moench
instrument: US equity indices (and major international equity indices)
original_claim_summary: US equity indices earned large, statistically significant average excess returns in the 24 hours preceding scheduled FOMC announcements from 1994-2011, accounting for a disproportionate share of total annual equity returns; no comparable effect was found in Treasuries or around other major macro news releases.
claimed_mechanism: pre-scheduled-event drift: prices drift upward ahead of a known, dated monetary policy announcement independent of its content
context: scheduled FOMC meeting days, 1994-2011 sample; effect specific to equities, not Treasuries or money-market futures
prerequisite_state: an FOMC meeting scheduled within the next 24 hours
event_sequence: FOMC meeting date approaches -> equity index drifts upward in the preceding 24-hour window -> drift resolves around/after the announcement
trigger: entering the 24-hour window before a scheduled FOMC announcement
invalidation: no measurable excess drift in equities during the pre-FOMC window relative to comparable non-FOMC 24-hour windows
claimed_outcome: positive average excess equity return concentrated specifically in the pre-announcement window
falsification_condition: If the average equity return in the 24 hours before FOMC announcements were statistically indistinguishable from random 24-hour windows, the claim would be false.

source_title: Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle
author_if_known: Anna Cieslak, Adair Morse, Annette Vissing-Jorgensen
timeframe: bi-weekly, keyed to FOMC meeting cycle
original_claim_summary: The entire US equity risk premium is earned in even-numbered weeks (0, 2, 4, 6) of FOMC cycle time, i.e. weeks starting from the most recent FOMC meeting, with odd weeks showing statistically insignificant average excess returns.
claimed_mechanism: cyclical liquidity/policy-communication pattern tied to the roughly six-week FOMC meeting cadence, not a specific announcement-day effect
context: measured relative to elapsed weeks since the last scheduled FOMC meeting, across the full sample period studied
prerequisite_state: elapsed time since last FOMC meeting is an even number of weeks (0, 2, 4, or 6)
event_sequence: FOMC meeting occurs -> weeks 0/2/4/6 from that meeting show concentrated equity risk premium -> intervening odd weeks show flat average returns
trigger: calendar alignment with an even FOMC-cycle week
invalidation: equity premium spread evenly across all FOMC-cycle weeks rather than concentrated in even weeks
claimed_outcome: statistically significant positive average return in even FOMC-cycle weeks; near-zero average return in odd weeks
falsification_condition: If average returns in odd FOMC-cycle weeks were statistically indistinguishable from (or larger than) even-week returns in an updated sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: Stock Market Prices Do Not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test
author_if_known: Andrew W. Lo, A. Craig MacKinlay
instrument: NYSE/AMEX weekly index and individual stock returns
original_claim_summary: Variance ratios for weekly US equity index and portfolio returns are significantly greater than one at 2- and 4-week horizons, rejecting the random walk hypothesis in favor of positive short-horizon serial correlation; the authors attribute much of this to nonsynchronous trading and small-cap stocks rather than a simple exploitable pattern.
claimed_mechanism: short-horizon positive autocorrelation in aggregated equity portfolio returns, driven substantially by microstructure effects (nonsynchronous trading) rather than pure behavioral momentum
context: weekly return horizons for diversified equity portfolios, particularly small-cap-heavy indices
event_sequence: weekly returns are computed and their variance ratio measured against multiples of the base holding period -> ratio found significantly above 1 at 2-4 week horizons
trigger: computation of the variance ratio statistic at short (2-4 week) aggregation horizons
invalidation: variance ratio statistically indistinguishable from 1 at these horizons
claimed_outcome: rejection of the random walk null hypothesis; evidence of positive short-horizon serial correlation, with a caveat about non-trading-driven artifacts
falsification_condition: If the variance ratio at 2-4 week horizons were not statistically different from 1 in a given sample, the random-walk-rejection claim for that sample would be false.

source_title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
author_if_known: Rama Cont
original_claim_summary: Large price changes tend to be followed by further large price changes of either sign, producing slowly-decaying (long-memory) autocorrelation in absolute and squared returns, even though raw signed returns show negligible linear autocorrelation.
claimed_mechanism: volatility clustering: the magnitude of price changes is persistent even though their sign is close to unpredictable at short lags
context: documented across essentially all liquid markets, instruments, and time periods studied in the surveyed literature
prerequisite_state: a recent period of elevated absolute/squared returns
event_sequence: a large-magnitude price move occurs -> probability of subsequent large-magnitude moves (either direction) remains elevated for an extended period -> autocorrelation of |return| decays slowly over many lags
trigger: an above-average absolute return observation
invalidation: autocorrelation of absolute/squared returns decaying immediately to zero (i.i.d. magnitude process)
claimed_outcome: persistently elevated realized volatility following large moves, independent of the direction of the next move
falsification_condition: If the autocorrelation function of absolute/squared returns dropped to statistical insignificance within one or two lags across markets, the volatility-clustering claim would be false.

source_title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
author_if_known: Rama Cont
original_claim_summary: Asset return distributions are heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis relative to Gaussian) and exhibit a leverage-type asymmetry where downside volatility tends to be more pronounced than upside volatility of comparable magnitude.
claimed_mechanism: fat tails plus negative return-volatility correlation: large drawdowns coincide with sharper volatility increases than comparably sized rallies
context: documented broadly across equity and other asset return series; the asymmetry is more pronounced in equities than in some other asset classes
prerequisite_state: a negative return of meaningful magnitude
event_sequence: a negative price shock occurs -> subsequent realized volatility rises by more than it would after a comparable positive shock
trigger: occurrence of a large negative return
invalidation: symmetric volatility response to positive versus negative shocks of equal magnitude
claimed_outcome: asymmetric volatility expansion following down-moves relative to up-moves of the same size
falsification_condition: If volatility responded symmetrically to positive and negative shocks of equal size across a broad asset sample, the leverage-asymmetry claim would be false.

source_title: A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
author_if_known: Dong Lou, Christopher Polk, Spyros Skouras
timeframe: daily, split into close-to-open (overnight) and open-to-close (intraday) segments
original_claim_summary: Cross-sectional stock momentum returns are earned almost entirely during the overnight (close-to-open) session rather than the intraday (open-to-close) session, indicating the momentum premium is concentrated outside of continuous trading hours.
claimed_mechanism: session-specific return concentration: the same signal (past return ranking) produces returns that are segregated by trading session rather than spread evenly through the day
context: cross-sectional momentum-sorted portfolios of US equities
prerequisite_state: a stock's momentum rank (winner/loser) based on trailing past returns
event_sequence: portfolio formed on trailing momentum -> overnight session captures nearly all of the momentum premium -> intraday session contributes little to no momentum premium
trigger: holding a momentum-sorted long-short portfolio through the close-to-open window specifically
invalidation: momentum premium distributed evenly (or concentrated intraday) rather than overnight
claimed_outcome: overnight segment accounts for effectively all of the realized momentum strategy return
falsification_condition: If the intraday session contributed a comparable or larger share of total momentum-portfolio returns than the overnight session, the claim would be false.

source_title: A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
author_if_known: Dong Lou, Christopher Polk, Spyros Skouras
timeframe: daily, split into overnight and intraday segments
original_claim_summary: For several well-known return anomalies (value, profitability, investment, market beta, idiosyncratic volatility, equity issuance, discretionary accruals, share turnover) that earn a statistically significant premium intraday, an economically and statistically significant premium of the opposite sign appears overnight, largely offsetting the intraday effect.
claimed_mechanism: session-level sign reversal: whichever anomaly premium is earned during continuous trading tends to be counteracted by an opposite-sign premium overnight for the same signal
context: cross-section of US equities sorted on multiple established characteristics
prerequisite_state: a stock characteristic sort that produces a significant intraday anomaly premium
event_sequence: characteristic-sorted portfolio earns a premium intraday -> the same portfolio held overnight earns an offsetting premium of opposite sign
trigger: holding the same characteristic-sorted long-short portfolio across both sessions separately
invalidation: overnight and intraday premia for the same characteristic showing the same sign or no relationship
claimed_outcome: combined full-day premium is smaller than either session's premium in isolation, due to the opposing-sign offset
falsification_condition: If overnight and intraday premia for these characteristics moved in the same direction rather than opposing directions in an independent sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: A Theory of Intraday Patterns: Volume and Price Variability
author_if_known: Anat R. Admati, Paul Pfleiderer
instrument: NYSE stocks (e.g. Exxon 1981 data used in the original empirical illustration)
original_claim_summary: Trading volume and price volatility both exhibit a U-shaped pattern through the trading day, high near the open and close and comparatively low around midday, theoretically explained by discretionary liquidity traders concentrating their trades around periods when informed traders are also active.
claimed_mechanism: strategic clustering of discretionary liquidity trading around the open and close, which concentrates both volume and volatility in a U-shape
context: continuous double-auction markets with a mix of informed and discretionary liquidity traders
event_sequence: session opens -> concentrated liquidity trading and information-driven trading co-occur -> volume/volatility spike -> midday lull as discretionary traders defer -> volume/volatility rise again into the close
trigger: proximity to session open or close
invalidation: flat, non-U-shaped intraday volume/volatility profile
claimed_outcome: systematically elevated volume and price variability at the open and close relative to midday
falsification_condition: If measured intraday volume and volatility were flat or highest at midday rather than at the open/close, the claim would be false.

source_title: The Tactical and Strategic Value of Commodity Futures
author_if_known: Claude B. Erb, Campbell R. Harvey
original_claim_summary: Commodities whose futures curve is in backwardation (nearby contract priced above deferred contracts) have historically earned higher average returns than commodities in contango; a long-the-most-backwardated/short-the-most-contangoed portfolio outperforms a passive long-only commodity index.
claimed_mechanism: term-structure/roll-yield signal: the shape of the futures curve conditions the expected roll return and realized return of a commodity
context: cross-section of individual commodity futures ranked monthly by their term-structure slope
prerequisite_state: a measurable and persistent slope (backwardation or contango) in the futures curve for the commodity
event_sequence: commodities are ranked by curve slope -> long the most backwardated, short the most contangoed -> portfolio rebalanced periodically
trigger: monthly ranking/rebalancing based on the term-structure signal
invalidation: no meaningful average return difference between backwardated and contangoed commodities
claimed_outcome: positive average excess return to the long-backwardation/short-contango portfolio versus a passive benchmark
falsification_condition: If backwardated and contangoed commodities showed statistically indistinguishable average returns out of sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: The Tactical and Strategic Value of Commodity Futures
author_if_known: Claude B. Erb, Campbell R. Harvey
original_claim_summary: Combining a trailing 12-month price momentum signal with the term-structure (backwardation/contango) signal produces higher average returns and improved risk-adjusted performance in commodity futures than using either the momentum or term-structure signal alone.
claimed_mechanism: signal complementarity: momentum and term structure capture different, partly independent sources of predictability in commodity futures returns
context: monthly-rebalanced commodity futures portfolios sorted by combined signal
prerequisite_state: both a trailing 12-month return ranking and a term-structure ranking available for each commodity
event_sequence: commodities double-sorted on momentum and term structure -> combined long/short portfolio formed -> rebalanced monthly
trigger: monthly double-sort and rebalance
invalidation: combined signal performing no better than the better of the two single signals
claimed_outcome: higher average return and/or better risk-adjusted return for the combined double-sorted portfolio versus single-signal portfolios
falsification_condition: If the combined momentum+term-structure portfolio did not outperform the better single-signal portfolio out of sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: Cultural Calendars and the Gold Drift: Are Holidays Moving GLD ETF?
author_if_known: Radovan Vojtko, Cyril Dujava
timeframe: daily, windows around dated cultural/religious festivals
original_claim_summary: Gold (via the GLD ETF) shows a statistically detectable positive price drift in the days surrounding major wealth-oriented cultural and religious festivals across Christian, Islamic, Hindu, and East Asian calendars, attributed to anticipatory physical/gift-related demand rather than standard risk-factor exposure.
claimed_mechanism: calendar-anchored demand shock: recurring, dateable cultural events generate anticipatory buying pressure in gold ahead of the event date
context: windows surrounding specific festival dates (e.g. Diwali, Eid al-Adha, Lunar New Year, Christmas) across multiple cultural calendars, aggregated globally
prerequisite_state: an approaching date on one of the studied cultural/religious calendars associated with gift-giving or wealth rituals
event_sequence: festival date approaches on a relevant calendar -> anticipatory demand builds -> GLD exhibits positive drift in the pre-festival window -> drift dissipates after the date passes
trigger: calendar proximity to a designated festival date
invalidation: no measurable abnormal drift in the GLD price window around the festival dates relative to comparable non-festival windows
claimed_outcome: positive abnormal drift in gold prices concentrated in the pre-festival window, described by the authors as persisting after controlling for standard risk factors
claimed_horizon: days to weeks around each festival date
falsification_condition: If GLD showed no statistically significant abnormal drift around the studied festival dates relative to matched control windows, the claim would be false.

source_title: Cultural Calendars and the Gold Drift: Are Holidays Moving GLD ETF?
author_if_known: Radovan Vojtko, Cyril Dujava
timeframe: daily, windows around dated cultural/religious festivals
original_claim_summary: This is a near-duplicate of SRC-acad-021 (same underlying paper, presented as a Quantpedia blog summary rather than the SSRN working paper) -- unlike festival effects previously documented in local equity or currency markets, the gold festival drift is described as pervasive across national borders because gold trades as a globally accessible, low-correlation safe-haven asset.
claimed_mechanism: cross-border demand aggregation: because gold is a single globally-traded asset (unlike locally-listed equities), festival-driven demand from many separate cultural calendars superimposes onto one price series
context: aggregated across multiple simultaneous or near-simultaneous festival calendars worldwide
prerequisite_state: overlapping or clustered festival dates across more than one cultural calendar
event_sequence: multiple culturally-distinct festival demand shocks occur close together on the calendar -> their gold-buying effects aggregate into a larger combined drift than any single festival alone
trigger: calendar clustering of festival dates from different cultural traditions
invalidation: no additional drift observed when multiple festival windows overlap versus a single isolated festival window
claimed_outcome: larger aggregate drift during periods of overlapping global festival demand than during isolated single-festival periods
falsification_condition: If overlapping multi-calendar festival windows showed no larger gold drift than isolated single-festival windows, the claim would be false.

source_title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
author_if_known: Mathias Mesfin
original_claim_summary: A 5-minute opening-range-breakout long signal on MNQ futures failed to clear realistic round-trip transaction costs out of sample: gross edge across tested configurations ranged roughly 0.07-1.50 points per trade versus an assumed 2-point round-trip friction, and the signal did not reach a T-statistic of 2.0 with consistent direction across 2021-2025 walk-forward folds.
claimed_mechanism: breakout-continuation failure: a range breakout at 5-minute resolution does not carry enough directional edge to survive realistic execution costs, contradicting a naive breakout-continuation assumption
context: single-bar, publicly observable OHLCV-derived opening-range-breakout signal tested with pre-registered walk-forward out-of-sample validation on a liquid index futures contract
prerequisite_state: opening range established and price breaking beyond it, exactly as in a standard ORB rule
event_sequence: opening range forms -> breakout triggers long entry -> position held per rule -> realized gross edge measured against fixed per-trade friction across 2021-2025 out-of-sample folds
trigger: breakout of the defined opening range
invalidation: a version of the signal clearing the pre-registered T-stat, trade-count, cost-hurdle, cross-year-consistency and permutation-test bar simultaneously
claimed_outcome: the ORB-long signal, along with 13 other single-bar OHLCV signal families tested, failed to produce a net-of-cost, statistically robust edge; edge only appeared when using regime classification and multi-bar holding structures rather than a raw single-bar trigger
falsification_condition: If the same ORB-long rule on MNQ produced a net-of-cost T-statistic >= 2.0 with consistent sign across 2021-2025 folds and passed the permutation test, this falsification claim itself would be false (i.e. the signal would in fact have edge).

source_title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
author_if_known: Mathias Mesfin
original_claim_summary: Across 14 tested single-bar OHLCV signal families (including gap-continuation and range/volatility-based reversal classifiers), none simultaneously satisfied all five pre-registered falsification criteria (T-stat >= 2.0, >=30 trades per fold, positive net-of-friction returns, consistent direction 2023-2025, and permutation p < 0.001); two positive-control signals (RTH confluence and a London-session signal) were included specifically to validate that the testing framework could detect real edge when present.
claimed_mechanism: systematic overstatement of naive single-bar technical signals: apparent edge in simple OHLCV-derived setups is generally an artifact of look-ahead, small samples, or unaccounted friction rather than a robust, persistent phenomenon
context: walk-forward, out-of-sample, pre-registered falsification framework applied uniformly to all signal families on one liquid futures contract
prerequisite_state: a fully specified, single-bar directional OHLCV trading rule
event_sequence: signal rule specified in advance -> tested walk-forward out of sample across multiple years -> evaluated against a fixed, pre-registered pass/fail bar -> compared to positive-control signals known/expected to show edge
trigger: application of the pre-registered falsification battery to a candidate signal
invalidation: a candidate signal other than the positive controls clearing all five criteria simultaneously
claimed_outcome: widespread failure of naive single-bar OHLCV signals to demonstrate robust, cost-adjusted edge, contrasted with the positive-control signals which the framework was able to validate
falsification_condition: If most of the 14 tested signal families had in fact cleared all five pre-registered criteria, the claim of widespread signal failure would be false.

source_title: Quantifying Volatility Compression and Expansion: A Predictive Model for Momentum-Driven Market Dislocations
author_if_known: Sanjay Manamala
instrument: generic/multi (equity and index instruments used in the model illustration)
timeframe: not fully specified in available abstract; appears to be daily/intraday squeeze detection
original_claim_summary: A quantitative volatility-compression detector ("squeeze" conditions, i.e. a contraction in realized/implied volatility relative to its own recent history) tends to precede explosive, momentum-driven directional price dislocations, and this transition can be modeled and partially predicted.
claimed_mechanism: volatility compression preceding expansion: a measurable narrowing of a volatility measure relative to its recent range raises the conditional probability of a subsequent large directional move
context: periods where a volatility-compression metric falls to a low percentile of its own recent history
prerequisite_state: volatility-compression metric (e.g. relative range/ATR contraction) at a low level versus recent history
event_sequence: volatility compresses ('squeeze' forms) -> compression persists for a detectable period -> a momentum-driven expansion/dislocation follows
trigger: the compression metric crossing a defined low threshold
invalidation: compression periods not followed by above-average subsequent volatility/directional expansion versus a matched control sample
claimed_outcome: elevated probability and/or magnitude of a subsequent directional price dislocation following detected compression
claimed_horizon: not fully specified in available materials
falsification_condition: If detected volatility-compression periods were not followed by above-average subsequent directional expansion relative to a matched non-compressed control sample, the claim would be false.

source_title: Volatility Regime Transitions and Equity Return Decoupling: Empirical Evidence from VIX Compression-to-Expansion Dynamics
author_if_known: Fabio La Manna
instrument: S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), 1993-2025
original_claim_summary: Around VIX compression-to-expansion regime transitions, the information content is primarily in the volatility domain rather than the equity-return domain: a VIX squeeze-to-expansion event does not reliably imply a directional equity drawdown, contradicting the conventional narrative that rising implied volatility after compression signals falling equity prices.
claimed_mechanism: decoupling of volatility-regime transitions from directional equity returns: implied-volatility compression-to-expansion is informative about future volatility level but not about the sign of the subsequent equity move
context: regime-based framework applied to daily SPY/VIX data over a multi-decade sample (1993-2025)
prerequisite_state: VIX identified as being in a compressed regime prior to the transition
event_sequence: VIX compression regime persists -> VIX transitions into an expansion regime -> subsequent SPY returns are examined for directional bias
trigger: a classified VIX regime transition from compression to expansion
invalidation: VIX compression-to-expansion transitions reliably preceding negative equity returns of a consistent magnitude
claimed_outcome: no reliable directional (bearish) equity signal from the VIX regime transition alone; the transition instead conveys information mainly about future volatility level
claimed_horizon: not fully specified in available abstract
falsification_condition: If VIX compression-to-expansion transitions were shown to reliably precede negative SPY returns of consistent sign and magnitude across the sample, the decoupling claim would be false.
